newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down in active trading on Wednesday on weak market sentiment triggered by poor overnight performance on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 21,250 yuan ($2,561) per tonne, losing 290 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 21,390 and hit a low of 21,150.
January fell 110 to 21,180, February 230 to 21,020, March 180 to 21,130, May 310 to 21,330, June 300 to 21,350 and July 220 to 21,480.
Combined volume rose to 93,370 tonnes from 71,440.
Copper opened lower and fell further before short-covering pushed the contracts off their lows.
Traders said the overnight LME correction following the failure to breach a key resistance level discouraged Shanghai's long position holders.

"Many investors believe copper will consolidate down in the next few days following the poor performance on the LME," one trader said. "Weak market sentiment resulted in little follow-up buying today."
But some traders said copper was not likely to fall sharply in the short term due to mixed opinions about the future market trend.
"Heavy short-covering later in the session indicated some investors were not very pessimistic about the future market trend," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to find strong support at around the 21,000-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. The January contract fell 90 to 14,660 yuan per tonne and February 100 to 14,900.
Combined volume fell to 1,450 tonnes from 1,980.
